title: Inference path fanning during high-concurrency bursts - retro and guardrails
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: During a traffic spike on 2025-02-13 the inference runtime started 'fanning' requests across multiple execution paths for mixed-quant attention models. That fanning behavior amplified probe traffic and caused KV-cache warmup contention, which produced a sustained p95 latency regression (1.8x) for 30 minutes across a subset of chat routes. This ticket captures the retro, root cause analysis, mitigation performed during the incident, and follow-up guardrails to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-13 09:03 UTC - First alert from synthetic p95 monitor; 09:07 - Ops page opened; 09:12 - Identified increased kernel probe rate coincident with high concurrent small-chat sessions; 09:18 - Scoped to mixed-quant attn model group and to two shards in us-west; 09:29 - Emergency mitigation: applied temporary probe rate cap + disabled speculative pathing for affected shards; 09:40 - Latency returned to baseline; 10:15 - Post-incident sampling and heap of logs archived to S3 for deeper analysis.
root_cause: A combination of factors: 1) recent scheduler tweak lowered the probe cooldown between kernel path probes to improve average throughput; 2) mixed-quant model variants have divergent kernel preference heuristics causing repeated probing under high concurrency; 3) KV-cache warmup coupled with small-batch requests caused resource contention so probes delayed cache population, amplifying tail latency. No single code crash; systemic amplification.
mitigation: Immediate: capped probe frequency and turned off speculative multi-path probing for affected shards. Medium term: roll back the probe cooldown change to previous value in runtime-1.18 branch while we implement safer probing. We also deployed a temporary throttle in the SDK for small-batch chat routes to reduce concurrent spikes.
action_items: Ben Ortiz: Implement probe backoff policy (exponential cooldown with jitter) in the scheduler and add unit tests. Target branch: runtime-1.19. Estimate: 5 points.
Clara Ng: Add a runtime metric for 'probe amplification' (probe_count/request_window) and a p95 alert threshold. Create dashboard and runbook entries. Estimate: 2 points.
Diego Ruiz: Build a mixed-quant canary job that runs representative chat workloads and records kernel-path diversity and p95. Wire into CI so regressions block canary gates. Estimate: 3 points.
Evan Park: Implement KV-cache warmup priority for small-batch chat sessions to prefetch likely prefixes during bounded quiescent windows. Prototype design due 2025-02-21. Estimate: 5 points.
Aisha Kumar: Coordinate SLA communication and customer outreach for impacted tenants. Draft sent to comms and legal. Due 2025-02-18.
QA Team: Add a synthetic benchmark for high-concurrency small-batch mixed-quant workloads with noise injection. Add to nightly regression suite. Owner: Priya Shah. Estimate: 4 points.
decisions: Rollback the recent probe cooldown reduction for the general runtime until probe backoff is implemented and validated.
Introduce a 'probe amplification' telemetry signal and automatic soft-throttle if amplification exceeds threshold for >60s.
Require canary coverage for any scheduler heuristic change that touches probe cooldown or kernel probing logic.
Treat mixed-quant model variants as a distinct class in scheduler heuristics to avoid cross-variant probe oscillation.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: stronger probe backoff reduces ability to rapidly discover faster kernels on workload shifts; decided to favor stability for p95-sensitive chat routes and expose a per-route override for aggressive probing.
Operator playbook updated to include 'probe amplification' as a triage knob and to run the canary job when making scheduler changes.
We observed two customer tenants with increased error budgets; follow-up with account teams completed and documented in comms thread.
